types.name: AIIntegration
types.description: AIIntegration represents an integration with an AI/LLM provider

fields.name: id
fields.description: The unique ID for managing the integration within Spacelift.

fields.name: space
fields.description:
Details of the space this AI integration belongs to.
Null for Spacelift-provided integrations.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The friendly name of the integration.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Optional description of the integration.

fields.name: labels
fields.description: User-defined labels set on the integration.

fields.name: provider
fields.description: AI provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Bedrock).

fields.name: providerIntegrationId
fields.description: ULID of the underlying provider integration (e.g. AWS integration for Bedrock).

fields.name: providerIntegrationName
fields.description: Friendly name of the underlying provider integration (e.g. AWS integration name for Bedrock).

fields.name: providerConfig
fields.description: Provider-specific configuration. Concrete shape depends on the provider.

fields.name: baseURL
fields.description:
Custom base URL for self-hosted OpenAI-compatible / Anthropic / Google
gateways (e.g. LiteLLM). Empty means use the provider default.
Not used for Bedrock integrations.

fields.name: models
fields.description:
Models explicitly pinned on this integration. Null means the integration
follows the provider's default model list; modelDetails reports what that
resolves to. For Bedrock integrations this is never null: it lists the
inference profile IDs stored on the integration, with no live AWS lookup.

fields.name: modelDetails
fields.description:
Models available on this integration with display names. For Bedrock
integrations, names are resolved live from AWS, which may fail or return
fewer entries than `models`.

fields.name: tokenUsage
fields.description: Account-level AI token usage for the current budget window.

fields.name: isSpaceliftProvided
fields.description: Indicates this is a Spacelift-managed integration that is read-only and visible to all accounts.

fields.name: enabled
fields.description:
Whether the integration can be used for LLM calls. Disabled integrations
remain visible and editable but are rejected by the AI provider proxy.
Spacelift-provided integrations read as disabled while the account has
Spacelift Intelligence off. Turning it on restores the account's last
choice for each one.

fields.name: allowedActions
fields.description: AI integration actions the current user is allowed to perform on this integration.

types.name: AIIntegrationTokenUsage
types.description: AIIntegrationTokenUsage represents account-level AI budget usage values.

fields.name: totalTokens
fields.description: Total budget tokens available in the current window.

fields.name: usedTokens
fields.description: Total budget tokens consumed in the current window.

fields.name: tokensResetAt
fields.description: Unix timestamp when the current budget window resets.

types.name: AIModel
types.description: AIModel represents a model available on an AI integration or provider.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Canonical model identifier (e.g. "claude-sonnet-4-6") or, for Bedrock integrations, the inference profile ID.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Human-readable display name for the model.

types.name: ModuleShareSpace
types.description:
ModuleShareSpace is a deliberately restricted projection on a Space. It exposes
only non-sensitive fields.
A module share is visible to users in the TARGET space, who may have no access to the SOURCE space.
Using the full `Space` type here leaked source-space details (description, labels, inheritEntities,
access rules) to those principals regardless of their access level, because
Space's field resolvers do not gate on access level. Narrowing the type makes
the sensitive fields impossible to query.
See https://app.clickup.com/t/869dzpd8k

fields.name: openTofuMigrate
fields.description:
Enqueues OpenTofu vendor migration (or rollback) for every stack that matches
the given search filter. The mutation is asynchronous.

The target argument determines direction:
- target=OpenTofu: migrate matching legacy stacks (vendor=Terraform,
  workflow_tool=OPEN_TOFU) to native OpenTofu vendor.
- target=Terraform: roll back previously migrated stacks to the legacy shape.

When triggerRun=true, the drain queues a tracked run on each stack after it
successfully migrates — useful for validating the new vendor against the
customer's existing configuration.

Stacks already in the target state, already in the queue, or in conflict
are silently skipped.

fields.name: openTofuMigrationQueueClean
fields.description:
Removes all pending (TO_MIGRATE / TO_ROLLBACK) entries from the migration
queue. Already-processed entries (MIGRATED, ROLLEDBACK, FAILED) are not affected.

commit currently tracked by a Stack or, if the Stack is not yet tracking any
commit, against the HEAD of the Stack's tracked branch. These defaults can
be overridden.

fields.name: runTriggerBatch
fields.description:
Trigger runs for multiple stacks as a single batch with a shared dependency tree.
For tracked runs, downstream dependents are resolved across all input stacks together,
so a shared dependent only gets a single run.
The output contains the runs created for the requested stacks as well as any runs
created for their dependents, in no particular order — correlate results to the input
via each run's stack rather than by position. A run's full details are only exposed
when you have read access to its stack; otherwise only its id is returned.

types.name: ObservabilityProcessingStatus
types.description:
ObservabilityProcessingStatus says how far a run's observability data got
through the pipeline that produces it.

enumValues.name: NOT_ELIGIBLE
enumValues.description: NOT_ELIGIBLE means the run will never produce this data.

enumValues.name: NOT_ELIGIBLE_TERRAFORM_VENDOR
enumValues.description:
NOT_ELIGIBLE_TERRAFORM_VENDOR is a subtype of NOT_ELIGIBLE: the run uses
the Terraform vendor, which captures nothing.

enumValues.name: PARTIAL_DATA_AVAILABLE
enumValues.description:
PARTIAL_DATA_AVAILABLE means the run has not finished, but it already
produced some data that can be shown to the user.

enumValues.name: PROCESSING
enumValues.description:
PROCESSING means the data has not landed yet, and is expected. The run
has not finished just yet, or it finished recently and the pipeline still
has work to do on it.

enumValues.name: AVAILABLE
enumValues.description: AVAILABLE means the data is stored and can be read.

enumValues.name: UNAVAILABLE
enumValues.description:
UNAVAILABLE means the data should be there and we cannot find it. Usually
the processing window has passed, so something went wrong: the pipeline
failed somewhere, or the run never uploaded anything.

types.name: OpenTofuMigrationCounts
types.description:
Headline counters for the Terraform -> OpenTofu migration. Account-wide: these
ignore any predicates the queue view has applied, so a filtered list will not
add up to them. Per-state counts that follow the filter come from
openTofuMigrationQueueSearchSuggestions instead.

fields.name: eligibleToMigrate
fields.description:
Stacks eligible for migration that are not queued right now — exactly what
openTofuMigrate(target: OpenTofu) with no predicates would enqueue, and the
same cohort openTofuMigrateSearch(target: OpenTofu) lists. Covers stacks
with no queue entry as well as ones whose last attempt ended in a terminal
ROLLEDBACK or FAILED state, since those can be re-driven.

fields.name: queuedToMigrate
fields.description: Queue entries in state TO_MIGRATE: picked up, not yet processed.

fields.name: queuedToRollback
fields.description: Queue entries in state TO_ROLLBACK: rollback requested, not yet processed.

fields.name: migrated
fields.description:
Queue entries in state MIGRATED: successfully migrated to native OpenTofu
and not rolled back since.

fields.name: rolledBack
fields.description:
Queue entries in state ROLLEDBACK: rolled back to the legacy Terraform
shape. Normally also counted in eligibleToMigrate, since a rolled-back
stack can be migrated again.

fields.name: failed
fields.description:
Queue entries in state FAILED: the migration or rollback errored, see the
entry's issues. A failed *migration* is normally also counted in
eligibleToMigrate, since re-issuing openTofuMigrate re-drives it. A failed
*rollback* is not: the stack still has vendor OpenTofu, so it belongs to
the rollback cohort, not the migration one. FAILED is a single state for
both directions, so this counter and eligibleToMigrate never have to move
together.

types.name: OpenTofuMigrationFailedIssue
types.description: The migration or rollback failed. Only a FAILED entry has it.

If you're running OpenTofu 1.10+, concise flag will be also used in apply.

fields.name: searchRuns
fields.description:
Paginated, account-wide run history ordered newest-first.
Scope the window with a TimeInRange predicate on the `createdAt` field.

Orderable by `createdAt`, `triggeredBy` and `state`. Ordering by `state`
follows the internal state ordinal, so equal states group together but the
sequence is not alphabetical.

`command` is only set on Tasks. It returns no possible values, so match it
with `fullTextSearch` or a `stringMatches` predicate.

Paginate with either input.after (keyset cursor, sequential) or offset
(random-access, for loading pages concurrently), not both. offset skips
that many rows in the ordered result; use input.first as the page size and
SearchRunsOutput.total to compute the page count.

Offset paging trades keyset's stability for random access, so pages can
skip or repeat rows if runs are created or deleted mid-scan.

types.name: RunMinutesTotals
types.description:
Minutes that ran on a worker, split by whether that worker belonged to the
public (default) pool. Only executing run states count: a run waiting in the
queue has no worker assigned, so its minutes are recorded as private, and
counting them would report queue time as private worker time. That filter is
why these two numbers sum to less than dailyByRunType / dailyByRunState.

fields.name: publicMinutes
fields.description: Minutes that ran on the public (default) worker pool.

fields.name: privateMinutes
fields.description: Minutes that ran on a private worker pool.

types.name: RunMinutesUsage
types.description:
Run-minutes are state durations - the time between consecutive run state
transitions - so a run contributes minutes to every state it passes through,
not just the ones that occupy a worker. A duration counts in full against the
day its state *started*; it is never split across day boundaries. A state
entered at 23:50 and left 20 minutes later puts all 20 minutes on the earlier
day, so a day's minutes can include time that elapsed later. Terminal states
never appear: they have no next transition, hence no duration.

fields.name: window
fields.description:
The window this response actually covers: the requested startTime/endTime
after endTime was capped at the start of today. Read the series against
these bounds, not the ones you sent - they can differ.

fields.name: dailyByRunType
fields.description:
Run-minutes per day, broken down by run type. One entry per (day, runType)
that has minutes; days with no runs are absent.

fields.name: dailyByRunState
fields.description: Run-minutes per day, broken down by run state.

fields.name: totals
fields.description:
Window totals split by worker-pool visibility. Counts executing run states
only, so these do not add up to the totals of the two series above - see
RunMinutesTotals.

types.name: RunMinutesUsageInput
types.description:
Window to report run-minutes over, half-open as [startTime, endTime). Both bounds
are unix seconds and must be midnight UTC - a whole multiple of 86400 - because the
rollup is per-UTC-day. A bound that is not midnight is rejected rather than rounded,
so being a few hours off cannot silently drop a day. The span may be at most 62 days.

inputFields.name: startTime
inputFields.description:
Inclusive lower bound. Days older than the rollup's retention horizon
(~183 days) hold no data and report zero.

inputFields.name: endTime
inputFields.description:
Exclusive upper bound, clamped to the start of today: the rollup only
covers days that have closed, so today is never reported. A window entirely
in the future is not an error - it reports an empty window and no data.

fields.name: start
fields.description: Unix seconds at midnight UTC, inclusive.

fields.name: end
fields.description: Unix seconds at midnight UTC, exclusive.

enumValues.name: MAJOR

fields.name: traces
fields.description:
The status of the OTEL spans the run's workers captured. A phase's trace
is complete once that phase ends, so a run that is still going reports
PARTIAL_DATA_AVAILABLE here once it stored its first span.

fields.name: metrics
fields.description:
The status of the metrics derived from those spans. A run that is still
going reports PARTIAL_DATA_AVAILABLE here once it stored its first metric
point, and AVAILABLE only after it reaches a terminal state.

types.name: RunState
types.description: RunState represents a discrete state of a Run.

enumValues.name: UNKNOWN
enumValues.description: An invalid "zero-value" for the run state.

enumValues.name: QUEUED
enumValues.description:
The run is queued and is either waiting for an available worker or for the
stack lock to be released by another run.

enumValues.name: CANCELED
enumValues.description: The run has been canceled by the user.

enumValues.name: INITIALIZING
enumValues.description: The run's workspace is currently initializing on the worker.

enumValues.name: PLANNING
enumValues.description: The worker is planning the run.

enumValues.name: FAILED
enumValues.description: The run has failed.

enumValues.name: FINISHED
enumValues.description: The run or task has finished successfully.

enumValues.name: UNCONFIRMED
enumValues.description:
The run has planned successfully, it reports changes and is waiting for the
user to review those.

enumValues.name: DISCARDED
enumValues.description: The run's plan has been rejected by the user.

enumValues.name: CONFIRMED
enumValues.description:
The run's plan has been confirmed by the user. The run is now waiting for
the worker to pick it up and start processing.

enumValues.name: APPLYING
enumValues.description: A worker is currently applying the run's changes.

enumValues.name: PERFORMING
enumValues.description: The worker is currently performing the task requested by the user.

enumValues.name: STOPPED
enumValues.description: The run has been stopped by the user.

enumValues.name: DESTROYING
enumValues.description:
The worker is currently performing a destroy operation on the managed
resources.

enumValues.name: PREPARING
enumValues.description: The workspace is currently being prepared for the run.

enumValues.name: PREPARING_APPLY
enumValues.description: The workspace is currently being prepared for the change deployment.

enumValues.name: SKIPPED
enumValues.description: The run was skipped.

enumValues.name: REPLAN_REQUESTED
enumValues.description: The run is pending a replan and should get picked up by the scheduler.

enumValues.name: PENDING
enumValues.deprecationReason: This state is no longer used.

enumValues.name: PREPARING_REPLAN
enumValues.description: The run is being prepared to be replanned.

enumValues.name: READY
enumValues.description: The run is ready to be started.

enumValues.name: PENDING_REVIEW
enumValues.description: The proposed run is waiting for post-planning approval policy sign-off.

fields.description:

but backend will accept `null` as input where this value is needed.

fields.name: terminal

fields.name: timestamp

fields.name: id

inputFields.name: forceApply
inputFields.description:
Controls behavior when a run's plan shows zero changes.
SINGLE: force-apply this run only, do not propagate to dependents.
CASCADE: force-apply this run and all triggered dependents.
Null means normal behavior (runs with no changes stop at the plan stage).

fields.name: runs
fields.description:
The runs created by the batch trigger: one per requested stack plus any
dependency-triggered runs, in no particular order.

fields.name: runId
fields.description: The ID of the created run. Always present, even for runs on stacks you cannot access.

fields.name: run
fields.description:
The created run. Only present when you have read access to the run's stack,
otherwise null. Dependency-triggered runs may land on stacks you cannot access.

inputFields.name: stack
inputFields.description: The stack (or module) slug.

inputFields.name: commitSha
inputFields.description:
Commit SHA to use. Defaults to the commit currently tracked by the stack,
or to the HEAD of the tracked branch if the stack is not yet tracking any commit.
For tracked runs, the stack's tracked commit will be updated to this commit.

fields.description: Provider of the stacks' repository.

types.description:
RunWithStack is a run together with the stack (or module) it belongs to, so
the account-wide runs view can render stack details without a separate
per-stack query.

fields.name: stack
fields.description: The stack (or module) the run belongs to.

fields.name: isModule
fields.description:
Whether the run belongs to a module. Surfaced here because the Stack type
does not expose it.

fields.name: outcome
fields.description:
Summary of how the run ended, available independently of findings.
Null if the summary could not be retrieved.

fields.name: findings
fields.description:
Observations excluding the outcome. Empty when evaluated with no findings;
null when not yet available or retrieval failed. Retrieval failures do not
produce GraphQL errors. Multiple findings may share a type; order is not
guaranteed.

types.name: RunWorkerMetrics
types.description:
A run's worker metrics grouped by what they describe, each measurement next
to the stack comparison it can be judged against. These are measurements
only: whether a value is slow is for the reader to decide, and whether the
metrics are complete is what `observabilityStatus.metrics` says.

fields.name: duration
fields.description:
Wall-clock time the run spent on the worker: final for a finished run,
elapsed so far for one still going. Waits between worker executions
are not counted. The P95 is drawn from runs that applied and finished.

fields.name: states
fields.description:
One entry per run state that either this run or the comparison runs
measured, in execution order. A state the worker does not trace has no
entry.

fields.name: slowestProviders
fields.description:
The providers the run spent the most time installing, longest first. The
run only reports the slowest few providers. Being at the top is not a
verdict: the slowest provider of a fast run is not a slow provider.

fields.name: comparison
fields.description: The population the P95 values were drawn from.

fields.name: windowDays
fields.description: Days before the run's creation that comparison runs were drawn from.

fields.name: runCount
fields.description:
Number of comparison runs: the population a comparison could be drawn
from.

fields.name: requiredRunCount
fields.description:
Number of comparison runs a p95 needs before it is published. Below it
every `p95Seconds` is null.

types.name: RunWorkerMetricsDuration
types.description:
A measured duration next to its stack comparison. Either side can be missing
on its own: a run that has not measured yet has a P95 but no seconds, a stack
with too few readings of this measurement has seconds but no P95.

fields.name: seconds
fields.description: This run's reading.

fields.name: p95Seconds
fields.description:
95th percentile of the same reading across the comparison runs. Null
unless there are at least `RunWorkerMetricsComparison.requiredRunCount`
data points.

fields.name: p95Ratio
fields.description:
Ratio of this run's seconds to the p95Seconds. Null whenever either
seconds or p95Seconds is null.

fields.name: p95Severity
fields.description:
Severity of the duration. Judged on `p95Ratio`. Null whenever
`p95Ratio` is null.

fields.name: runState
fields.description:
The run state the resources failed in, one of the values
`RunWorkerMetricsState.runState` takes.

fields.name: resourceType
fields.description: Resource type as the workflow tool names it, such as `aws_s3_bucket`.

fields.name: count
fields.description:
Resources that failed, summed over every run state and resource type. A
resource counts once per state it failed in, however many times it
failed there.

fields.name: breakdown
fields.description:
The same count by run state and resource type, in execution order then
by type.

fields.name: command
fields.description:
The hook's command line as the worker reports it, such as `./seed.sh`.
A hook can be a whole inline script, so a long command line is cut.

fields.name: phase
fields.description:
`before` or `after`, saying whether the hook ran before or after the
command of its run state.

fields.name: durationSeconds
fields.description:
Time the state spent on this hook, summed over every time the state ran
it in this phase.

types.name: RunWorkerMetricsInput
types.description: Selects the comparison window for `Run.workerMetrics`.

inputFields.name: comparisonWindowDays
inputFields.description:
Days before the run's creation that comparison runs are drawn from, 1
through 90. Defaults to 30.

fields.name: address
fields.description:
Provider source address as the workflow tool reports it, such as
`registry.opentofu.org/hashicorp/aws`.

fields.name: installDurationSeconds
fields.description:
Time spent installing the provider, summed over every run state that
installed it.

fields.name: address
fields.description:
Resource instance address as the workflow tool reports it, such as
`aws_s3_bucket.main` or `module.web.aws_instance.this[0]`.

fields.name: resourceType
fields.description: Resource type as the workflow tool names it, such as `aws_s3_bucket`.

fields.name: durationSeconds
fields.description:
Time the state spent on this instance, summed over every operation it
performed on it. A plan state that both reads and refreshes an instance
reports the two together.

fields.name: failed
fields.description: Whether this resource reported an error for this instance.

fields.name: runState
fields.description:
One of INITIALIZING, PLANNING, APPLYING, DESTROYING and PERFORMING, the
run states the worker traces.

fields.name: failed
fields.description:
Whether this run ended in FAILED after an error occurred while executing
this state.

fields.name: errors
fields.description:
Error details for this failed state, in the order the worker reported
them. Empty when the state did not fail or no details were captured.

fields.name: slowestResources
fields.description:
The resource instances this state spent the most time on, longest first.
The state only reports the slowest few resources. Being at the top is
not a judgement: the slowest instance of a fast state is not a slow
resource. Null for a state that never works on resources, such as
INITIALIZING. Empty for a state that can, but reported none.

fields.name: slowestHooks
fields.description:
The user hooks this state spent the most time on, longest first. The
state only reports the slowest few hooks. Null for a state that never
runs hooks. Empty for a state that can, but reported none.

fields.name: message
fields.description: The exception message, as the worker redacted it.

fields.name: resourceAddress
fields.description:
Resource instance address the error came from, such as `aws_s3_bucket.main`
or `module.web.aws_instance.this[0]`. Null when the error is not tied to a
single resource.

fields.name: title
fields.description:
How the run ended, in a few words: "Finished", "Stopped", "Failed
during planning".

fields.name: description
fields.description:
The note on the run's final state transition, such as the reason it
failed. Null when there is no note.

fields.name: category
fields.description:
How well the run did. Null for a finished run until
`observabilityStatus.metrics` is AVAILABLE.

types.name: RunWorkerOutcomeCategory
types.description: The categories go from best to worst.

enumValues.name: Healthy
enumValues.description:
The run finished with a normal duration and has no findings. There is
nothing to do.

enumValues.name: Finished
enumValues.description:
The run finished with a normal duration and has at least one finding,
so there is something to improve.

enumValues.name: Slow
enumValues.description:
The run finished, but took much longer than the stack's P95, in total
or in one of its states. This is the same rule that gives a duration
the MAJOR severity.

enumValues.name: Interrupted
enumValues.description:
The run ended before it could finish or fail: it was stopped, canceled,
discarded or skipped.

enumValues.name: Failed
enumValues.description: The run ended in FAILED, no matter which state it failed in.

fields.description: How many runs the warning window holds in total, ignoring the cap on runs.

fields.name: skipReplanWhenRunAll
fields.description:
If set to true, the apply phase will reuse the plan from the planning phase instead of
re-planning. Only applies when useRunAll is enabled.
Runs with disabled useRunAll reuse the plan by default.

WARNING: this means any mocked_outputs referenced during planning will be applied as-is.
Do not enable this together with mocked_outputs unless you fully understand the implications —
your apply may execute against mocked values rather than real ones.

DEPRECATED: use skipReplan instead, which works for both run-all and non-run-all stacks.
fields.deprecationReason: Use skipReplan instead, which applies to both run-all and non-run-all stacks.

fields.name: skipReplan
fields.description:

re-planning. Successor of skipReplanWhenRunAll, applies to both run-all and non-run-all stacks.

WARNING: this means any mocked_outputs referenced during planning will be applied as-is.
Do not enable this together with mocked_outputs unless you fully understand the implications —
your apply may execute against mocked values rather than real ones.

fields.name: prefixResourceNamesWithModuleName

types.name: StackSpaceAccessGrantSource
types.description: How a grant reaches the queried space, i.e. where its space sits relative to it.

enumValues.name: RESIDENT
enumValues.description: The grant lives on the queried space itself.

enumValues.name: PROPAGATED
enumValues.description:
The grant lives on an ancestor space and reaches the queried space by
propagating down.

enumValues.name: INHERITED
enumValues.description:
The grant lives on a descendant space and reaches the queried space by
inheritance up the tree (the descendant chain has inherit_entities enabled).

types.name: StackSpaceAccessRoleGrant
types.description: A role grant giving a stack access to a space, either directly or through the space tree.

fields.name: role
fields.description:
The role effective on the queried space. For INHERITED grants only read
climbs up an inherit_entities edge, so this is the synthetic "Space reader"
system role, which may differ from binding.role (the bound custom role).

fields.name: source
fields.description: How this grant reaches the queried space (resident, propagated, or inherited).

fields.name: binding
fields.description:
The explicit binding backing this grant. Null for the implicit self-read
every stack has on its own home space. For INHERITED grants it names the
originating custom role and descendant space the read climbed from, so
binding.role intentionally differs from the effective role above.

types.name: StackState
types.description:
StackState represents a discrete state of a Stack, which is also the state of
its most currently running Run.

enumValues.name: NONE
enumValues.description: No tracked run has been started yet, so the stack has no meaningful state.

enumValues.name: INITIALIZING
enumValues.description: The current tracked run is now initializing.

enumValues.name: PLANNING
enumValues.description: The current tracked run is now planning.

enumValues.name: FAILED
enumValues.description: The last tracked run has failed.

enumValues.name: FINISHED
enumValues.description: The last tracked run has finished successfully.

enumValues.name: UNCONFIRMED
enumValues.description: The current tracked run is awaiting human confirmation.

enumValues.name: DISCARDED
enumValues.description: The last tracked run has been discarded by the user.

enumValues.name: CONFIRMED
enumValues.description: The current tracked run has been confirmed by the user.

enumValues.name: APPLYING
enumValues.description: The current tracked run is now applying.

enumValues.name: STOPPED
enumValues.description: The last tracked run has been stopped.

enumValues.name: DESTROYING
enumValues.description: The current destroy job is now deleting all managed resources.

enumValues.name: PREPARING
enumValues.description: The current tracked run is now preparing for execution.

enumValues.name: PREPARING_APPLY
enumValues.description: The current tracked run is now preparing to apply the change.

enumValues.name: REPLAN_REQUESTED
enumValues.description: The current tracked run is pending a replan.

enumValues.name: PREPARING_REPLAN
enumValues.description: The current tracked run is being prepared to be replanned.

enumValues.name: READY
enumValues.description: The current tracked run is now ready for execution.

enumValues.name: BUSY
enumValues.description: Worker is currently processing a worker.

enumValues.name: DRAINED
enumValues.description: Worker is not accepting new work.

fields.name: cycle
fields.description: Billing cycle selected by `cyclesAgo`. An omitted value selects 0.

fields.name: selectableCycles
fields.description:
Every cycle `cyclesAgo` can select right now, newest first, starting with
the current cycle. The list stops at the oldest retained cycle or at the
cycle the account was created or the contract started in, whichever is
newer. Past dates are extrapolated from the current contract, and the list
shifts by one when a new cycle starts.

fields.name: daily
fields.description:
One point per day in the selected cycle. The current cycle runs through
today; a past cycle includes every day. Days without activity return zero.
Pass `percentiles` to populate `concurrencyAtPercentilesToDate`. Each value
must be between 0 and 100, and a query may request up to 5 values. Omit
`percentiles` to skip those calculations.

fields.name: concurrencyPercentiles
fields.description:
Private worker concurrency at each requested percentile. The current
cycle covers elapsed time; a past cycle covers its full duration. Results
preserve request order. Each value must be between 0 and 100, and a query
may request up to 5 values.

fields.name: concurrencyAtContractedPercentile
fields.description:
Concurrency at the percentile the contract bills on (contractedPercentile).
Null when there is no contract or the contract has no percentile, matching
contractedPercentile.

fields.name: contractedLimit
fields.description:
Worker concurrency limit in the current contract. Null when the account
has no contract or no limit. Past cycles also use this current value,
which may differ from the limit in effect during that cycle.

fields.name: multiAccountContract
fields.description:
True when contractedLimit is not specific to this account: other accounts
draw on the same limit, so this account's usage is only part of what counts
against it.

fields.name: contractedPercentile
fields.description:
Billed percentile in the current contract, such as 95. Null when the
account has no contract. Past cycles also use this current value.

fields.name: burst
fields.description: Null unless the contract has both a limit and a percentile.

types.name: WorkerUsageBurst
types.description:
Uses the current contract's limit and percentile, including for past cycles.
`budgetMinutes` applies the current billed percentile to the selected cycle's
duration.

fields.name: budgetMinutes
fields.description: How many minutes of the full cycle may exceed the contracted worker limit.

fields.name: usedMinutes
fields.description:
Minutes above the current contracted limit. The current cycle counts time
elapsed so far; a past cycle counts its full duration. Each minute counts
once, regardless of how far concurrency exceeded the limit.

fields.name: remainingMinutes
fields.description: budget - used (may be negative when over).

fields.name: cyclesAgo
fields.description: The `cyclesAgo` value that selects this cycle.

fields.name: start
fields.description: Unix seconds, inclusive.

fields.name: end
fields.description: Unix seconds, exclusive on the minute timeline.

fields.name: day
fields.description: Unix seconds at midnight UTC.

fields.name: max
fields.description: Peak concurrent workers that day.

fields.name: concurrencyAtContractedPercentileToDate
fields.description:
Concurrency at contractedPercentile computed cumulatively from the cycle
start through the END of this day, so the last point equals
concurrencyAtContractedPercentile. Null exactly when contractedPercentile
is null. Unlike max, this excludes the live tail, so on the current day it
can lag by a couple of minutes.

fields.name: concurrencyAtPercentilesToDate
fields.description:
Concurrency at each percentile requested via daily(percentiles:), computed
cumulatively from the cycle start through the END of this day - so the last
point matches concurrencyPercentiles for the same input. Returns exactly the
requested percentiles, in request order; empty when none were requested.
Like concurrencyAtContractedPercentileToDate, this excludes the live tail.

fields.name: burstMinutesUsed
fields.description:
Minutes of THIS day, not cumulative, in which worker concurrency exceeded
contractedLimit. Summed over the cycle this equals burst.usedMinutes. Null
exactly when contractedLimit is null; 0 means the day stayed within the
limit. Excludes the live tail, like the percentile above.

types.name: WorkerUsageInput
types.description:
Selects the billing cycle returned by `workerUsage`. Omitting `input`, passing
an empty input, omitting `cyclesAgo`, and setting `cyclesAgo` to 0 all select
the current cycle.

inputFields.name: cyclesAgo
inputFields.description:
Number of billing cycles before the current cycle. Null means 0. 0 selects
the current cycle to date; 1 selects the most recent completed cycle.
Valid values range from 0 through 5.

The rollup retains the current monthly partition and the six preceding
partitions. An anniversary-based billing cycle can span two partitions,
so selecting cycle 6 could read a dropped partition as zero.

A past cycle that ends before the account was created, or before the contract
or subscription started, returns an error. The cycle those dates fall in stays
selectable. The current cycle is never checked. A valid cycle older than the
rollup returns zeros, which is indistinguishable from no usage.

fields.name: percentile
fields.description: Which percentile this is, e.g. 95

fields.name: value
fields.description: Concurrent workers at that percentile

types.name: __Directive
types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type validation behavior in a GraphQL document.

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution behavior
in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally including or
skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing additional information
to the executor.

types.name: __DirectiveLocation
types.description:
A Directive can be adjacent to many parts of the GraphQL language, a
__DirectiveLocation describes one such possible adjacencies.

enumValues.name: QUERY
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a query operation.

enumValues.name: MUTATION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a mutation operation.

enumValues.name: SUBSCRIPTION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a subscription operation.

enumValues.name: FIELD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment definition.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_SPREAD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment spread.

enumValues.name: INLINE_FRAGMENT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an inline fragment.

enumValues.name: SCHEMA
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a schema definition.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a scalar definition.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an object type definition.

enumValues.name: FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field definition.

enumValues.name: ARGUMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an argument definition.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an interface definition.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a union definition.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an enum definition.

enumValues.name: ENUM_VALUE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an enum value definition.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an input object type definition.

enumValues.name: INPUT_FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an input object field definition.

types.name: __EnumValue
types.description:
One possible value for a given Enum. Enum values are unique values, not a
placeholder for a string or numeric value. However an Enum value is returned in
a JSON response as a string.

types.name: __Field
types.description:
Object and Interface types are described by a list of Fields, each of which has
a name, potentially a list of arguments, and a return type.

types.name: __InputValue
types.description:
Arguments provided to Fields or Directives and the input fields of an
InputObject are represented as Input Values which describe their type and
optionally a default value.

fields.name: defaultValue
fields.description: A GraphQL-formatted string representing the default value for this input value.

types.name: __Schema
types.description:
A GraphQL Schema defines the capabilities of a GraphQL server. It exposes all
available types and directives on the server, as well as the entry points for
query, mutation, and subscription operations.

fields.name: types
fields.description: A list of all types supported by this server.

fields.name: queryType
fields.description: The type that query operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: mutationType
fields.description: If this server supports mutation, the type that mutation operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: subscriptionType
fields.description: If this server support subscription, the type that subscription operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: directives
fields.description: A list of all directives supported by this server.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of
types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that
type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name and description, while
Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields
they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types
possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an interface. `fields` and `possibleTypes` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.

directives.name: deprecated
directives.description: Marks an element of a GraphQL schema as no longer supported.

args.name: reason
args.description:
Explains why this element was deprecated, usually also including a suggestion
for how to access supported similar data. Formatted in
[Markdown](https://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/).

directives.name: include
directives.description: Directs the executor to include this field or fragment only when the `if` argument is true.

directives.name: skip
directives.description: Directs the executor to skip this field or fragment when the `if` argument is true.

directives.name: specifiedBy
directives.description: Provides a scalar specification URL for specifying the behavior of custom scalar types.

args.name: url
args.description: The URL should point to a human-readable specification of the data format, serialization, and coercion rules.
